name: Critical minerals
summary: China extended its pause on rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan 2027 on 9 Nov; April 2025 licensing remains in force
state: On 9 Nov China's commerce ministry extended its suspension of export controls on some critical minerals to 10 Jan 2027, formalising a truce extension before it lapsed, and suspended a 24% tariff on US goods for two months (The National). Licensing requirements imposed in April 2025 on seven heavy rare earths remain, so Watch holds. Trump and Xi are expected to meet at APEC in Shenzhen on 18–19 Nov; no production stoppages outside China linked to bans were found as of 13 Nov.
for_you: Makers of magnets, motors, electronics and defence equipment outside China remain exposed to licence delays and short-notice policy changes; the current pause runs only to 10 Jan 2027.
rubric_hit: Licensing in force on seven heavy rare earths (Watch); no export-ban stoppages outside China (Alert not met)

sources.title: The National — China extends pause on rare earth export curbs for two months

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
